$comment: The five roads on /start (client/src/pages/Start.tsx), one for each person the site is for, and the row of chips on Home that opens them (/start#<id>). Each road is four to six steps in order, one sentence and one link each, and every link is a page that exists and is public today. A step names the page and why it comes next; it promises nothing and teaches nothing. The 'new' road is the six steps /start has carried since 2026-11, unchanged; its 'track' names the track that road has become (client/public/tracks/, held to the tracks index by start.test.tsx), which /start offers as the road's main action with the six steps kept under it. 'next' and 'quiz' follow the 'new' road. 'pages' are the two readers no road fits, found by the walk of 2026-11-23 (docs/work/elite/walk-2026-11.md): the Christian with doubts and the pastor or group leader. Each is one card on /start and one chip on Home that opens the one page to begin with, by that page's own title ('link'), not a road, so neither is a track to be written. 'order' is the order of the cards and the chips, roads and pages together. scripts/prerender-heads.mjs reads this file for the page's crawlable list and for Home's static chips, and start.test.tsx checks every link and count against the site's own data.

pages.link: I'm not sure I believe anymore

pages.chip: I'm a pastor or group leader

steps.title: For skeptics
steps.line: Start on the page made for people who don't believe, where the questions are laid out before anyone argues anything.

steps.title: Does God actually exist?
steps.line: Most people begin with this question, so read the short answer next and note where you would push back.

steps.title: Did the resurrection happen?
steps.line: Christians say their faith stands or falls on this event, so it is the claim to test after that.

steps.title: Test the Case
steps.line: Here you weigh the evidence one case at a time and decide where you land on each.

steps.title: Read a Gospel for yourself
steps.line: Mark is the shortest of the four, so read the source itself, with notes beside every chapter.
steps.link: Open Mark in the Study Bible

steps.title: Take eight weeks
steps.line: If you want to keep going, this plan takes the questions one week at a time.
steps.link: Eight Weeks for the Curious Skeptic

roads.title: New to faith, or coming back

steps.title: Read the Gospel of John
steps.line: John has twenty-one chapters, so a chapter a day takes three weeks, and the Study Bible has notes on every one of them for the parts you don't follow yet.
steps.link: Open John in the Study Bible

steps.title: Learn to pray
steps.line: If nobody ever taught you how to pray, begin with five minutes a day and the prayer Jesus gave his followers, one line at a time.
steps.link: Eight Weeks of Learning to Pray

steps.title: Find a church
steps.line: This faith was never meant to be lived alone, so look for a faithful church, which isn't the same thing as a perfect one, and go more than once before you decide.

steps.title: Walk the first eight weeks
steps.line: Eight Weeks for a New Christian gives each week one focus, one small daily practice and one thing to read, and it gets to baptism, the old habits, and the doubts that come back.
steps.link: Eight Weeks for a New Christian

steps.title: Learn what Christians believe
steps.line: The catechism teaches the faith in seventy-six short questions and answers, from "Who made you?" onward, and each one has an answer for an adult and a shorter one for a child.

steps.title: Go through it with someone
steps.line: New Believers is a five-session study on your first steps of faith, and it comes with a leader's guide, so you can ask a friend or a pastor to sit down and do it with you.

roads.title: If you've stepped back from faith

steps.title: If a church hurt you
steps.line: If a church is part of why you stepped back, start with the page written for that, before anything else here.

steps.title: If you're taking it apart
steps.line: This page is written for someone working through what they were taught, one question at a time.

steps.title: Done with church, not with Jesus?
steps.line: Many people land here, so read the short answer next and see whether it names where you are.
steps.link: Done with church but not Jesus?

steps.title: What comes after
steps.line: This answer looks at what people build once the old version has come apart.

steps.title: The longer story
steps.line: The faith is older than any one church you knew, and the history course follows it from the apostles to today.

steps.title: Take eight weeks
steps.line: If you want company for the questions, this plan takes them one week at a time.
steps.link: Eight Weeks of Taking Your Questions Seriously

roads.title: If you want to go deeper

steps.title: Read a whole book
steps.line: Open the Study Bible and read one book straight through, with notes on every chapter beside the text.

steps.title: Learn how each kind of book reads
steps.line: A letter, a psalm and a prophecy are read differently, and these guides show how before you go further.

steps.title: Take the history course
steps.line: The course follows the church from the apostles to today, one lesson at a time.

steps.title: Study a doctrine
steps.line: Then take what the Bible teaches one topic at a time, with the passages behind each.

steps.title: Read the creeds
steps.line: These are the words the church has confessed together, in their own text.

steps.title: Weigh where Christians differ
steps.line: Last, set the views side by side on the questions faithful Christians still disagree about.

steps.title: Tonight's devotion
steps.line: Start with one devotion at the table tonight: a passage, a question to talk about, and a prayer.

steps.title: The family catechism
steps.line: Next, learn one short question and answer together, and stay on it as long as it takes.

steps.title: A reading plan
steps.line: When the table has a rhythm, a plan gives you a passage a day and keeps your place.

steps.title: Every devotion
steps.line: Keep the whole library close for a hard night, a season, or a question that came up.

steps.title: Bible Explorer
steps.line: For a child between 7 and 16, the Explorer lays the whole Bible out as one story on a single illustrated map, with short moving pictures to watch together.

steps.title: For the parents
steps.line: This study is for the grown-ups, on handing the faith to the children in your house.
